=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/guard_differential.py:282-309 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: parse_loosening_policy documents in the module docstring (line 33-40) and the shipped policy file that the policy format is {"version": 1, "exceptions": [...]}, but line 290 reads document.get("exceptions") without ever reading or checking document.get("version"). A missing version key, a mistyped version such as "1" instead of 1, or a future-bumped version such as 2 is silently accepted under v1 rules.
  WHY: If the policy schema evolves with new mandatory fields or changed entry semantics, a v2 policy committed to the base branch would be silently parsed under v1 rules, potentially misinterpreting loosening entries without any operator-visible error. The function is documented as "strictly validate" and the version key is part of the documented format, so it should fail closed on a missing, mistyped, or unsupported version.
- scripts/guard_differential.py:798-814 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The --json output row at lines 801-813 includes tree, hook, line, shape, base, head, loosened, intended, and pr_body_listed, but omits approved_by. The text output for intended_loosening rows at line 795-796 does include approved_by via json.dumps(result.approved_by). A JSON consumer can see that a shape was policy-approved via intended=true but cannot identify who approved it.
  WHY: The JSON output loses the audit-trail link that the text mode provides. Any downstream tool that consumes --json output cannot determine whether an approval came from the policy (approved_by set) or was absent, and cannot attribute approvals to specific operators. The field exists on the ShapeResult dataclass at line 162 but is not serialized.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/guard_differential.py:282-309 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The function docstring at lines 42-47 documents the policy format as `{"version": 1, "exceptions": [...]}` and promises "strict validation", but the implementation never reads `document.get("version")`. A policy with `version` missing, with `version: "1"` (string), with `version: 2`, or with `version: null` is silently accepted under v1 rules. The shipped file `.github/guard_differential/intended_loosening.json` carries `{"version": 1, "exceptions": []}`, so this is a load-bearing contract that the parser does not enforce.
  WHY: A future v2 policy with different field semantics (e.g. a new mandatory field, a `kind` discriminator, an array-of-shapes `shape` field) would be silently parsed under v1 rules — entries dropped, misinterpreted, or false-passed — and the operator would see no error. The malformed-policy test list at tests/test_guard_differential.py:286-299 has no case for `{"exceptions": [...]}` without `version` or with `version: 2` / `version: "1"`, so the regression is not caught. The trust boundary the PR just established (issue #5326) is undermined at the first schema bump. The minimal fix is ~3 lines: after the dict check, require `document.get("version") == 1` (rejecting missing, wrong-int, and string-typed versions) and raise SetupError with the source path.
- scripts/guard_differential.py:798-814 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The JSON row dict emits `intended`, `pr_body_listed`, `loosened`, `head`, `base`, etc. but omits `approved_by`, which is present on the ShapeResult dataclass at lines 159-160 and is printed in the text-mode `intended_loosening` line at line 796 (`approved_by={json.dumps(result.approved_by)}`). A consumer reading the JSON can see that a shape was policy-approved (`"intended": true`) but cannot determine who approved it.
  WHY: For any JSON-driven audit (CI log aggregation, downstream dashboards, the #5326 threat model itself), the approver identity is the link back to the operator who signed off on a guard weakening. Text-mode keeps that link, JSON-mode drops it, and the two modes are documented side-by-side in agents.md:1247-1252 as the same contract. The shipped dataclass field already exists; this is a one-line addition to the JSON dict. The existing test `test_current_hooks_are_deterministic_against_themselves` (tests/test_guard_differential.py:768-781) exercises `--json` but only checks `row["base"] != row["head"]`, so the gap is not caught by current coverage.
- Requirement: "After this change the PR body is data only. A loosening is excused only by an entry in `.github/guard_differential/intended_loosening.json` read from the base ref. The entry must name the hook, the verbatim corpus shape, and the PR's head commit." (PR description, Summary)
  Expected change site: scripts/guard_differential.py:282-309 (parse_loosening_policy)
  Evidence of absence: The parser validates hook, shape, head_sha, approved_by, reason on each entry, but does not validate the documented `{"version": 1, "exceptions": [...]}` envelope. Without `version` enforcement, a future schema change silently regresses the same trust boundary the PR is closing. The malformed-policy test list in tests/test_guard_differential.py:286-299 lacks `{"exceptions": [...]}` without `version` and lacks `version: 2`, so the gap is shipped without coverage.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/guard_differential.py:288-292 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The function never reads or validates the documented mandatory top-level `version` field. The module docstring (lines 38-40) and the shipped policy file both declare the format as `{"version": 1, "exceptions": [...]}`, and the function's own docstring says it "strictly validate[s]" the policy. But `document.get("version")` is never checked. A policy with `{"version": 2, "exceptions": [...]}` or `{"exceptions": [...]}` (no version at all) is silently parsed under v1 rules.
  WHY: If the policy schema evolves (new mandatory fields, changed entry semantics) and a publisher bumps the version, this parser accepts the v2 document without error and interprets entries under v1 rules. The malformed-policy test suite (`test_parse_loosening_policy_rejects_malformed_policies`) covers missing `exceptions`, bad `head_sha`, bad `hook`, etc., but has no case for a missing or wrong `version`. The fix is one line after the dict check: `if document.get("version") != 1: raise SetupError(f"{source}: unsupported policy version {document.get('version')!r}")`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
